newsitem.title: USA: General Cigar sets specifics of IPO.
newsitem.headline: General Cigar sets specifics of IPO.

text.p: General Cigar Holdings Inc has set forth the specifics of its proprosed initial public offering, planning to offer six million shares in a range of $14 to $16 each, according to documents filed Tuesday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The company is the largest maker and marketer of cigars in the United States, according to its prospectus. It sells the two top selling premium cigars in the United States, Macanudo and Partagas, as well as other brands. The company also runs a cigar bar, "Club Macanudo" in New York City and plans to open one in Chicago in the spring of 1997.
General Cigar posted 1996 operating profit of $32.3 million on sales of $196.7 million, after giving effect to an acquisition.

Its parent company, Culbro Corp, will retain 97 percent of the voting power of the company by giving the Class A common stock limited voting power. Each Class A share will be worth only one vote, while each share of Class B stock, to be held by Culbro, will have 10 votes.

The offering is tentatively scheduled for the week of February 24, according to lead underwriter Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities. The shares will trade on the NYSE under the proposed symbol "MPP".
